title: sovereign ai
subtitle: what changed in the procurement guidance?
summary: A document comparison supporting an FOI follow-up: application windows, eligibility checks, notification wording and a reproducible evidence trail.
scope: Supporting evidence for a Freedom of Information request and a proposed follow-up. This page compares two published guidance files; it does not establish a breach of law, deliberate concealment or a failure to notify suppliers. The follow-up questions below are a draft, not a submitted request.
provenance: Based on two supplied PDFs and a draft comparison prepared on 18 October 2026. Text was independently extracted with Poppler, compared and checked against the PDFs. The original files have not been altered.

versions.verification: Local PDF, live URL download and supplied Wayback snapshot payload have identical SHA-256 hashes; checked 2026-10-19.
Local PDF, live URL download and supplied Wayback snapshot payload have identical SHA-256 hashes; checked 2026-10-19.

findings.title: full applications move to defined windows
findings.text: V1 allows approved suppliers to submit a Full Application at any time for the next assessment batch. V2 ties submission to Competition Dates, adds opening dates and repeats the window restriction in Stage 2. This establishes a wording change, not when the portal actually changed.

findings.title: stage 1 onboarding remains continuous
findings.text: Both versions still allow companies to apply to join the Approved Supplier List at any time (page 4). The follow-up should distinguish this onboarding from the later Full Application windows.

findings.title: notification is an unresolved evidence question
findings.text: Both versions promise page updates and email notification to approved suppliers. The requester reports not seeing an X or homepage announcement. This review has not audited historical posts, publication logs or supplier emails; it cannot conclude that nobody was notified.

unchanged_passages.title: stage 1: joining the approved supplier list
unchanged_passages.text: Companies may apply to join the Approved Supplier List at any time by completing our Expression of Interest (EOI) form on the Sovereign AI website.

unchanged_passages.title: the notification clause
unchanged_passages.text: Any changes will be updated via this page and suppliers on the ‘Approved Supplier List’ will be notified via email.

unchanged_passages.title: the subcontracting cap already existed
unchanged_passages.text: No more than 50% of the work can be subcontracted.

changes.title: full applications: from any time to competition dates
changes.before: Once you are an Approved Supplier, you can submit your Full Application at any time, and it will be assessed after the next competition deadline.
changes.after: Once you are an Approved Supplier you can submit your Full Application in line with the Competition Dates.
changes.analysis: V2 removes the express permission to submit at any time. Read this alongside the added opening dates and Stage 2 wording; the PDFs alone do not establish portal availability.

changes.title: three opening dates added
changes.after:
Opens 15 September 2026
Opens 14 November 2026
Opens 30 January 2027
changes.analysis: These opening dates are added for batches 1, 2 and 3. The listed submission deadlines and outcome dates are unchanged. The excerpts show the three added lines, not one continuous sentence.

changes.title: lead applicant work share added to eligibility
changes.after: The lead applicant must carry out at least 50% of the work.
changes.analysis: An explicit lead-applicant work-share condition appears in the eligibility checklist. Both versions already contain a 50% subcontracting cap on page 8; this is not evidence that the numerical cap was newly introduced.

changes.title: challenge selection added to stage 1 checks
changes.after: Which challenge you intend to address.
changes.analysis: V2 adds this item to the EOI checklist. V1 already required proposals to address a current challenge in its eligibility section, so challenge alignment itself is not new. The actual EOI form has not been compared.

changes.title: subcontracting confirmation added to stage 1
changes.after: Confirming your understanding that no more than 50% of the work can be subcontracted.
changes.analysis: The existing cap is now explicitly acknowledged at Stage 1. This is a change to the published checklist, not proof of how an individual application was assessed.

changes.title: competition windows repeated in stage 2
changes.before: Following admission to the Approved Supplier List, applicants can submit a proposal against any of our live competition challenges.
changes.after: Following admission to the Approved Supplier List, applicants can submit a proposal against any of our live competition challenges within the Competition Date windows.
changes.analysis: This reinforces change 01 in the Full Application instructions. It is a separate text edit, not a separate additional restriction.

changes.title: flexigrant portal description revised
changes.before: Applicants will be invited to submit their Full Application on Flexigrant, an application portal which contains detailed instructions on the assessment questions and information required at the Full Application stage.
changes.after: Applicants will be invited to submit their Full Application on Flexigrant, an application portal which contains instructions on the assessment questions and detailed information on each of the challenges.
changes.analysis: The description shifts emphasis to detailed challenge information. This comparison does not establish whether the portal’s content or questions changed.

changes.title: outcome timing: within one month becomes one month after
changes.before: You will receive an outcome within one month of the deadline.
changes.after: You will receive an outcome one month after the deadline.
changes.analysis: This may change the expectation of an earlier response; it should not be dismissed as necessarily cosmetic. The three specified outcome dates are unchanged. Intent and practical effect are not established by the PDFs.

changes.title: eligibility addressed directly to the applicant
changes.before: The proposal must address one of the Scheme’s current challenges.
changes.after: You must address one of the Scheme’s current challenges.
changes.analysis: The requirement remains to address a current challenge. The sentence now addresses the applicant directly.

foi_context: Mars Robertson submitted request FOI2026/02870 on 24 September 2026. It sought records about review, approval, feedback, conflicts of interest and the post-launch response. The request included an express fallback to approval and conflict-of-interest records, as well as a qualified request for readily identifiable information.

The department’s 16 October response says it holds the requested information but estimates that searches would exceed the £600 cost limit. It describes searches across mailboxes and SharePoint folders, acknowledges the refined wording and asks for it to be submitted as a new request. It also suggests narrowing document types, topic and period. See pages 5–6 of the response.

The response does not say that the words “where practicable” caused the refusal. Whether the handling of the fallback was adequate is a separate question; this comparison does not determine it. ICO guidance explains cost-limit refusals, advice and assistance, and treating refined requests as new requests. Removing a qualifier does not guarantee disclosure.

draft_foi.status: draft — not submitted by this site
draft_foi.intro: Please provide the following recorded information concerning replacement of the two Sovereign AI R&D Procurement Scheme guidance PDFs identified on this evidence page. For decision, publication and communication records, please limit the search to 28 August–19 October 2026. For policies, please provide the version applicable to that revision. I seek existing records, not a new explanation or analysis.
items: The policy or procedure in force for approving, versioning and publishing changes to guidance for this scheme, including any requirement to notify applicants or approved suppliers.

The final approval or decision record authorising this revision, and the publication/version-history entry showing when the revised PDF was first published or linked. Please include recorded approval dates and approving roles; personal names are not required.

The final notification text and any existing dispatch or publication log for this revision: notification date, channel and recipient category, including Approved Supplier List emails. Recipient email addresses are not requested. If a decision not to issue a notification is recorded, please provide that decision and its recorded reasons; this question does not assume that no notification was sent.

The final decision record or approved briefing recording the reasons for introducing opening and closing windows for Stage 2 Full Applications rather than accepting them continuously. Please include any recorded consideration of continuous Stage 1 onboarding, which both guidance versions retain.
draft_foi.closing: If a requested record is not held, please say so. If the request would exceed the section 12 limit, please identify the scope or searches responsible and provide section 16 advice on a specific narrower request likely to fall within it. I am willing to prioritise the publication record and final notification text. Please identify any exemptions relied on for withheld information.

method: V1 and V2 are comparison labels assigned here, not official version numbers. All page references use physical PDF pages, including V2’s unnumbered pages.

Local files were hashed with SHA-256. Downloads from both live URLs and both supplied Wayback snapshots matched the corresponding local file byte-for-byte on 19 October 2026. Hashes establish byte identity, not authorship, lawfulness or the first publication date.

Full text was extracted with pdftotext -layout, then compared with whitespace, page furniture and reflow distinguished from wording changes. Nine grouped wording edits are presented, not nine independent policy changes. The presentation is not a byte-level or exhaustive visual diff.

Key pages were rendered for visual checking. The move from 10 to 11 pages, lost printed page numbers and text reflow are layout differences, not additional policy changes. No wording change was identified in the challenge descriptions, assessment criteria, IP provisions or the notification clause in this text review.

The PDF creation timestamps are metadata, not proof of when wording was written, approved or published. V2’s timestamp is later than its listed first opening date; that fact alone does not prove a retrospective rule change. The archive captures provide dated access points, not necessarily the earliest publication.

The requester’s observation about announcements is attributed, not independently proved. Historical social posts, webpage publication logs, supplier emails, the live application portal and any private correspondence were not audited. No inference of deliberate concealment is made.

AI assisted the initial comparison and this review. Agreement between models is not verification. The linked PDFs, exact excerpts, hashes and recorded-information questions allow readers to check the evidence themselves.
